items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Well, when Jo came with the band -- see, Jo came in the band five or six months later, I came back, and I walked in one night and Basie was building the band.

ctx.x: So you played with Basie for awhile then, in '34?
Well, when Jo came with the band -- see, Jo came in the band five or six months later, I came back, and I walked in one night and Basie was building the band.

We're not talking about when Jo came in -- we're talking about this drummer, whose name we can't recall -- you set in at first. Did you ever work with him regularly, with Basie -- did you come in and play regular?

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was Jonathan Jones there? ... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, you see, I left -- this is '34 going on '35 -- I left after my first induction into the Reno Club...

ctx.x: Well of course, Jo Jones would be there, and then this other drummer whose name ...
Was Jonathan Jones there? What year was this when Jo was there?

Well, you see, I left -- this is '34 going on '35 -- I left after my first induction into the Reno Club, and this wonderful music, this wonderful band; when I came back six months later, I came back with all intentions, I'm improving as a kid and as a musician, and I'm still with Dan Murphy's Musical Skippers, going in on '35. I came back with all intentions of sitting down with this band, and really with my improved drumming, making a display of myself.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I knew him playing with Dan Murphy and his Musical Skippers. But Cliff got religion, he quit the band and stayed in Kansas City.

ctx.x: I worked last week with a drummer that I consider a very great drummer and a milestone in jazz history and he knows you very well and loves you dearly, and I'm sure you love him. But I'd like for you just to say something about him. His name is Cliff Leeman. He said he was around Kansas City when you were around there.

Cliff Leeman came from Dan Murphy's Musical Skippers all the way from Portland, Oregon. Cliff Leeman quit the band in Kansas City and he was a sub-drummer with the jump-up band that Basie had. Nobody ever heard that band to speak of but people like - when Woody Herman came in with Isham Jones, Jerry Jerome was playing across the street but Cliff Leeman was in the place before I'd get there because I was babysitting.
